overview: Build a nether portal with crying obsidian and the overworld around it starts to rot: grass to netherrack, water to lava, trees to crimson stems, and mobs into their nether counterparts.
Each crying obsidian block in the frame buys another 64 blocks of radius, so how far it goes is up to you.

1.2.2: A corrupted block keeps every property it shares with what it becomes, so torches stay on walls and panes keep hold of their neighbours.

Water within three blocks of anything lava could set alight is left as water: a pond by a house used to take the house with it. Lighting a frame with crying obsidian in it finally earns an advancement, since that is the whole mod in one act.
1.2.1: Crying obsidian frames light again after the game changed the way it checks a portal's shape.
1.2.0: With village-quests installed, a cleric hands you four stones with exactly one crying among them and points you at a half-built doorway a hundred and fifty blocks out. Far enough that what happens next never reaches the houses, which is the point: they are not being generous, they are being careful.
1.0.0: Crying obsidian portal frames spread corruption outward one block at a time, the way grass spreads, across more than two hundred block types.
Mobs standing on corrupted ground may turn: pig to zombified piglin, villager to zombie villager, slime to magma cube, horse to skeleton horse.
